overall_reason: The stock AI-SaaS landing page in full: violet-to-cyan aurora behind frosted glass panels, a pill eyebrow over a centred Inter headline, a fake terminal hero, three icon-circle feature cards, an unsourced four-figure stat band, three pricing tiers, a CTA band and a link-farm footer; the YAML and terminal details are plausible but sit on a default skeleton and a default look.

findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: hero with product mock (terminal panel) -> three equal feature cards -> stat band (99.99% / -42% / 12ms / 2.3M) -> code block -> three pricing tiers (Starter $0 / Team $49 / Enterprise Custom) -> closing CTA band ("Put your agents to work — with a leash.") -> link-farm footer (Product / Resources / Company). Six stock sections in stock order, plus the eyebrow-per-section rhythm.
findings.before: hero mock, 3 features, stats, config, 3 tiers, CTA band, footer
findings.after: Build the page around the one real artefact it has, the relay.yaml and a run trace: lead with a real trace and let features be annotations on it; cut the stat band and the CTA band
findings.why: Specific details on a default skeleton still read as a default page.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: violet blob top-left, cyan blob right, magenta radial bloom behind the terminal panel, every surface a translucent frosted card (13 containers share radius 20px + the same shadow). The sweep found the violet-gradient cluster on the brand mark; the screenshots show the aurora wash and glass are the whole page's ground, not one element.
findings.before: aurora mesh + glass panels on #1e1b4b-family ground
findings.after: One solid dark ground, panels drawn with a 1px rule rather than blur, colour reserved for the trace's status states (ok / retry / fail)
findings.why: Aurora-plus-glass is the most recognisable generated look for AI tools; it says 'AI startup' and nothing about Relay.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: "Ship agent workflows with confidence", "Everything your agents need, nothing they don't" and "Start free. Scale when you're ready." stay true with LangSmith, CrewAI or any agent platform's name. T-FRESH-READER generic lines: these three plus "Deploy in minutes, tune in days, trust from the first run."
findings.after: A head only Relay can say, built from its mechanism, e.g. "Every agent run gets a budget, a fallback and a trace."
findings.why: The hero and every section head are category boilerplate, so the first screen identifies a category, not a product.

findings.evidence: Sub-line says "Four primitives cover the full lifecycle of a production agent run" but only three cards follow (Intelligent routing, Full observability, Self-healing runs); the fourth slot in the row below is the stat band.
findings.after: Name the fourth primitive (the YAML shows budget caps: [DATA NEEDED: is budget enforcement the fourth primitive?]) or say "Three"
findings.why: A count that does not match what is shown is the mark of copy written before, or apart from, the layout.

findings.evidence: A styled-div terminal with traffic-light dots, "relay — session #4821", and invented run figures ("$0.28", "1,840 tokens", "2m 14s · $0.61 · p95 latency 12ms"). A 2m14s run reporting a p95 latency of 12ms reuses the stat band's "12ms p95 overhead" figure, so the mock and the stats share one invented number.
findings.before: drawn terminal with invented session data
findings.after: A real captured trace from the product, or [DATA NEEDED: a real run log]; drop the window dots
findings.why: Imitation product UI with invented figures is decoration posing as evidence.

findings.evidence: Icons are Unicode glyphs "⌁", "◉", "↻" in 54px translucent circles centred above each heading. T-DELETION: removing them loses nothing; "⌁" does not read as routing.
findings.before: glyph in a circle over each card title
findings.after: Remove the icon circles; if a visual is wanted, show a two-line trace snippet per feature
findings.why: Glyph-in-circle over every card is icon-tile filler (the sweep's icon_tile detector missed it because the glyphs are text).

findings.evidence: Pill labels above headings: "AGENT ORCHESTRATION · NOW IN GA", "WHY RELAY", "DROP-IN CONFIG", "PRICING"; all heads centred on one axis with the lede, two pill buttons and a note beneath (SLP-150 centred-everything hero). Pill buttons and a pill nav repeat the radius-999 recipe 7 times.
findings.before: pill eyebrow + centred h1 + centred lede + two pills
findings.after: Drop the pills; left-align the hero head with the trace beside it; one button shape
findings.why: The context the sweep's eyebrow hit lacks: the pill eyebrow is the frame of every section, so the page's rhythm is the template's rhythm.

strengths: The relay.yaml block is concrete and product-specific (budget hard cap, fallback models, degrade on tool failure, jsonl export); it is the one thing a rival could not copy and should lead the page.
Feature body copy names mechanisms ("Timeouts retry with backoff, failed tools degrade to fallbacks, and sessions resume from checkpoint.") rather than adjectives.
Pricing states real limits (100 runs/mo, 1 project, 2 agents) instead of vague tiers.
not_investigated: Whether Relay's metrics are real: no contract or supplied facts; treated as unsourced per INT-007 (already a sweep hit).
